the use of x ray absorption fine-structure spectroscopy (XAFS) to probe the structure of metal hydrides.
the use of x ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) to study metal hydrogen systems, in both the gas phase and in situ in an electrochemical cell.
the use of x ray absorption spectroscopy as a probe of the electronic structure of metal hydrides and the use of this technique as an in situ probe of electrochemical processes.

the L edge XAFS of the MmL 4.5 M 0.5 Al 0.5 (M=Ca,Mn) intermetallic metal hydride electrode material is a sensitive probe of the electronic structure of these materials, and that this sensitivity increases upon charging the battery.

the x ray absorption fine structures of the La, Ce, Nd, and Pr L edges in the MmL 4.5 Mn 1.5 intermetallics are sensitive to the electronic structure of the intermetallic and are therefore a useful probe of the electronic structure of this important class of intermetallics.

the x ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) technique is a very sensitive probe for the electronic changes occurring in intermetallic metal hydrides during electrochemical hydrogenation and is therefore an excellent technique for the study of these important materials.

the XANES of the MmL 3 intermetallic can be used to probe the electronic structure of the intermetallic compound in the presence of a hydrogen atmosphere, thus allowing the determination of the electronic structure of an intermetallic compound during its operation in a battery.
